newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa returns home on stretcher.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa returns home on stretcher.

text.p: Mother Teresa was released from hospital on Wednesday and taken back to her religious order after being given a clean bill of health, a doctor treating the revered Roman Catholic missionary said.

Eyes closed and hands folded, the 86-year-old nun, who was taken to hospital last week after falling from a chair, was carried on a stretcher into the Missionaries of Charity order where nuns greeted her with applause, witnesses said.

"God bless you," Mother Teresa said to Sister Frederica, the order's second-ranking nun, as she was carried into the Missionaries of Charity headquarters, her home in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta.

To the sound of the chapel bell, about 30 nuns surrounded Mother Teresa and danced in joy before she was taken to the order's prayer room, witnesses said. Later she was carried to her room where she was examined by a doctor, they said.
A doctor said Mother Teresa was carried on a stretcher because of longstanding back pain and not because of any lingering effects from the fall onto her head that she suffered on September 16.

"There is no cause for concern," said Dr A.K. Bardhan of Woodlands Nursing Home where she had undergone treatment. He said a brain scan earlier on Wednesday showed a blood clot detected last week had disappeared.
